newsitem.title: USA: Immunex Melanoma drug tests positive.
newsitem.headline: Immunex Melanoma drug tests positive.

text.p: SEATTLE, Wash., March 17 (Reute) - Immunex Corp said tests of its Leukine drug as a therapy following surgery showed a significant increase in the one-year survival rate of patients with advanced stages of malignant melanoma.

The company said the findings, which came out of an ongiong Phase II clinical trial, were presented over the weekend at the Second International Conference on the Adjuvant Therapy for Malignant Melanoma in London.
Based on the success of the trials to date, Immunex said it plans to proceed with Phase III trials.

The trials involved 30 patients, who showed a median survival of 20.6 months, compared with 11.2 months in a control group. Patients in the study had either advanced Stage III malignant melanoma involving multiple regional lypmh nodes, or Stage IV disease with widespread metasteses of the cancer.
Leukine, which stimulates the production of white blood cells, has been available in the U.S. since 1991 and is used to treat leukemia and other cancers.
